name: Mount Kenya
description: From bamboo thickets to alpine deserts, every step reveals a new world. The summit, Point Lenana, greets you with silence and sweeping sunrises.
summary: Bamboo belts, giant lobelias and a pre-dawn push to Point Lenana. The mountain I keep coming back to.
intro: I'd been circling this mountain for years, photographing it from the lowlands, watching its peaks catch first light from my Nairobi balcony. But being on it, inside its ecosystems, was entirely different. The camera became secondary to just being present in each moment.

What struck me most wasn't the summit, it was the in-between spaces. The way light filtered through bamboo forests at 3,000m. How silence feels different at altitude. The rhythm of walking for hours with only breath and footsteps.

itinerary.title: Sirimon Gate to Old Moses
itinerary.body: I began the hike before dawn, moving through a forest alive with unfamiliar sounds and a pack that felt too heavy. By the second hour I stopped counting steps and simply walked until Old Moses Camp emerged through the mist, cold, simple, perfect. Above 3,000 meters everything felt different: the air, the meal, the silence.

itinerary.title: Into Mackinder's Valley
itinerary.body: The landscape opened into something prehistoric with giant lobelias, and my guide pointed out Batian and Nelion as I tried and failed to capture their scale. Altitude hit at Shipton's with a dull headache and slow movements, but a quiet climb to Hausberg Col with just one lens forced me to really see.

itinerary.title: Summit Attempt and Gorges Valley Descent
itinerary.body: At 2:30am we started for the summit, the line of headlamps ahead looking like a prayer. Every step hurt, but Point Lenana at 6:15am with the sun rising over endless plains broke me open. The descent to Lake Michaelson and down to the bamboo forest felt like time travel.

fieldNote: Battery performance drops significantly above 4,000m. Cold drains them fast. Keep spares warm against your body. The α7R IV held up remarkably well, though I shot with gloves on most of summit day.
heroCaption: Between the clouds and the quiet

name: Mackinders Camp
description: A high-altitude sanctuary in the Teleki Valley. The trail challenges you with the infamous 'Vertical Bog' before rewarding you with iconic, close-up views of the Batian and Nelion peaks.
summary: Through the Vertical Bog to a camp sitting right under Batian and Nelion.
intro: A high-altitude sanctuary in the Teleki Valley. The trail challenges you with the infamous 'Vertical Bog' before rewarding you with iconic, close-up views of the Batian and Nelion peaks.

name: Likii North
description: A remote and scenic route on the northern side of Mount Kenya. It offers a quieter, off-the-beaten-path trekking experience through unique moorland landscapes and crystal-clear river crossings.

name: Elephant Hill
description: The ultimate test of endurance in the Aberdares. Famous for its thick bamboo forests, relentless mud, and the psychological hurdle known as the 'Point of Despair'.

name: Mount Kipipiri
description: A standalone volcanic cone detached from the main Aberdare range. Known as the 'butterfly' mountain, it offers long, beautiful forest walks and a rewarding, windy summit.
